claims.text: Applying a thin aluminum-rich coating to a refractory high-entropy alloy improves its high-temperature oxygen resistance.
The aluminum-rich coating promotes formation of a stable protective Al2O3 scale.
The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy is a multi-principal-element solid solution.
The untreated alloy has no preformed protective oxide layer.
The intervention produces a continuous Al2O3 scale on the alloy surface.
The Al2O3 scale produced by the intervention is adherent.
The Al2O3 scale produced by the intervention is crystalline.
The aluminum-rich coating oxidizes preferentially at high temperature.
Preferential oxidation of the coating forms a stable Al2O3 barrier.
The Al2O3 barrier limits oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
Limiting oxygen diffusion decreases further oxidation and degradation relative to the untreated alloy.
After exposure at 1100°C in ambient air for 100 hours, the coated alloy will have significantly lower weight gain than the untreated alloy.
After the specified exposure, the coated alloy will have a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
After the specified exposure, the coated alloy will retain better surface integrity than the untreated alloy.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically form rapidly growing mixed-oxide scales under the specified conditions.
The mixed-oxide scales typically formed by untreated refractory high-entropy alloys are non-protective.
The coating is expected to be effective around 1100°C under constant oxidizing atmospheres.
There is no direct evidence cited for the proposed coating treatment in the specific refractory high-entropy-alloy system.
The optimal coating thickness and deposition method are not established.
The coating's performance consistency across different refractory high-entropy-alloy compositions is not established.
